cohort: The study included 536,507 women who delivered livebirths in Ontario between April 2012 and November 2016, excluding those with delivery <24+0/7 weeks, major fetal anomalies, or preexisting renal disease.
finding: The introduction of the new definition of preeclampsia was associated with increased disease rates, a modest reduction in adverse neonatal outcomes, and no change in maternal outcomes.
followup_time: Neonatal period (outcomes at birth or shortly after)
gest_age: Livebirths <37 weeks, <34 weeks, <32 weeks (as outcomes); excluded deliveries <24+0/7 weeks
